title.narrative: Companies participating in cost-shared technology and services development activities (with emphasis on biomass and wind) by 2008.

comment.narrative: 45 companies participate in cost-shared technology and service development activities. The target for this indicator has beensurpassed. Among them, the proponents associated with wind power technology, biomass, and solar PV are 18, 14 and 4 respectively,there are also 9 companies involved in small hydropower technology.

title.narrative: 25MW straw-fired biomass power plant at Mabei Village, Rudong County, Jiangsu selling 162 GWh/year into local grid.

comment.narrative: Progress on the Rudong Biomass Power Plant is satisfactory. The plant has entered into operation, and generated 156 GWh and sold141 GWh to the grid in 2010.

title.narrative: Pipeline of renewable energy projects under development in the provinces by 2008 (MW capacity in pipeline)

comment.narrative: The target for the end of the Phase has already been achieved. CRESP supported the development of a number of renewable energyprojects, not financed by the World Bank loan. These include:7 projects under the Provincial Demonstration Project facility; 14projects under the Investment Scale-up Support Facility (ISSF); 1 tidal energy project in Zhejiang; 1 inter-tidal wind project inJiangsu; 1 offshore wind project in Zhejiang; 1 offshore wind project in Fujian.These projects constitute a pipeline of 5 windprojects witha total capacity of 500 MW, 2 biomass projects with a total capacity of 6 MW, one tidal energy project with a capacityof 20 MW and8small hydro projects with an incremental capacity of 17.4 MW.

title.narrative: 100MW wind farm at Changjiangao, Pingtan Island, Fujian selling 260 GWh/yer into local grid by 2008

comment.narrative: The wind farm has been in operation since 2008. In 2010, the wind farm generated 370 GWh

title.narrative: Improved quality and reduced cost among manufacturers and service providers in wind and biomass

baseline.value: No evidence that cost and quality is improved

target.value: Substantial evidence, through technical and soical

comment.narrative: There are around 40 wind turbine integrators, of which 20 produce MW scale wind turbines - a substantial increase from 2005. Thenumber of biomass boiler manufacturers increased from 1 in 2005 to 5 in 2008. There has been an overall improvement in quality ofwind and biomass equipments in China, particularly through support under CRESP.At present, the leading domestic wind turbinemanufacturers, in particular the proponents of CRESP, have received design certification by international certification bodies, andthey areworking on type certification as well, meaning that their products have met high international standards. CRESPsupported one ofthe proponents to implement the biomass gasification generation project which has the largest installation capacityin the world.Since 2008, the average price for wind turbine in China has decreased at an annual rate of around 1,000RMB/kW.Currently, the bidding price for concession has declined to approximately RMB 4,000/kW or even below.

title.narrative: Market framework in pilot provinces established through laws and regulations.

baseline.value: No evidence that market framework is in place

target.value: Renewable Energy Law (REL) enacted and Implementat

comment.narrative: There is ample evidence that a market framework has been established, not only in the provinces, but nationwide. The RE Law wasadopted in Feb. 2005, became effective in Jan. 2006 and was amended further in December 2010. It was complemented by rules andregulations, and targets set in the 11th FYP.

title.narrative: Environment for development of renewables improved

baseline.value: No evidence that the environment is improved

target.value: Substantial evidence, through technical and social

comment.narrative: The REL and related regulations provide the legal framework for the development of renewable energy, making project approvalprocedures clearer and more transparent. The outcome of strong government support for renewable energy development has been asignificantincrease in renewable electricity capacity and electricity production. Total RE capacity which already is 2.5 times morethan the target for the end of Phase 1.

title.narrative: Issuing of regulations for implementation of REL andtheir effective implementation in pilor provinces (Fujian, Inner Mongolia, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang) by 2009.

comment.narrative: Progress has been made nationwide, and has not remained limited to the pilot provinces. Renewable Energy Law and its implementingregulations are required to be implemented nationwide.

title.narrative: Issuing of regulations to implement the law at national level by 2009

comment.narrative: RE Law Amendment was adopted at the 12th Session of the Standing Committee of the 11th National People#s Congress on December 26,2009 and became effective on April 1, 2010.17 implementing regulations have been approved by ministry level authorities by 31December 2010). Law was passed. More have been developed as part of CRESP.

title.narrative: Issuing of national standards for wind turbines, availabiity of testing facilities and certification by 2009.

comment.narrative: 7 standards have been approved by the Standardization Administration of China (SAC) on November 10, 2010. The remaining one hasbeen submitted to SAC for approval in March, 2011, and it is expected that it will be approved before 30 September 2011. 2 windturbine testing centers are expected to be accredited to carry out power performance, power quality, acoustic noise and mechanicalload testing, which are the types of testing required for type certification.
